title: Lower limb & axial anatomy · Past year 2
note: 23-page screenshot compilation; cover shows a lower-limb examination dated 1399/11/13 but institutional provenance is not independently confirmed. Nineteen distinct questions survive; several lack source numbers. Full includes four spinal items and one general limb-development item; Lower only excludes these. Internal duplicate screenshots are counted once. Visible selections are not treated as an authenticated answer key.

questions.prompt: Which muscle inserts into the iliotibial tract?
questions.note: Gluteus maximus inserts partly into the iliotibial tract and partly into the gluteal tuberosity. Tensor fasciae latae also inserts into the tract but is not offered.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which artery is not normally a branch of profunda femoris?
questions.note: Descending genicular normally arises from the femoral artery near the adductor hiatus. Circumflex femoral origins vary, but profunda is their standard textbook origin.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle forms the lateral border of the femoral triangle?
questions.note: The medial border of sartorius forms the lateral boundary of the femoral triangle. Adductor longus forms its medial boundary; the inguinal ligament is superior.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The deep plantar arch is an anastomosis between dorsalis pedis and which artery on the sole?
questions.note: The deep plantar branch of dorsalis pedis joins the lateral plantar artery to complete the deep plantar arch; dorsalis pedis does not enter the sole as its entire trunk.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle is not innervated by a nerve of the sacral plexus receiving lumbosacral-trunk contributions?
questions.note: Sartorius is femoral nerve, L2-L3, from the lumbar plexus. The other choices are supplied through superior gluteal or sciatic/tibial pathways. The original calls these 'branches of the lumbar sacral trunk', although named peripheral nerves arise from the plexus, not directly from that trunk.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.sourcePrompt: Which of the following muscles is not innervated by a branch of the lumbar sacral trunk?

questions.prompt: Which listed nerve is most closely related to the small saphenous vein?
questions.note: The expected choice is C, referring to the medial sural cutaneous contribution and sural nerve. The standard companion of the small saphenous vein is the sural nerve; its formation and level of union vary. Do not treat medial sural cutaneous and the final sural nerve as universally identical.
questions.subject: anatomy
evidence: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26826266/ — sonographic study of sural nerve variants and small saphenous vein relationships.

questions.prompt: Which listed artery does not arise directly from the posterior tibial artery in the usual pattern?
questions.note: The distal perforating branch is a branch of the fibular artery, not a direct posterior tibial branch. Circumflex fibular origin varies (including posterior tibial or anterior tibial origins), so the standard teaching pattern is specified.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle is traditionally called the peripheral heart?
questions.note: Soleus is the conventional answer because its venous sinuses and contraction contribute to the calf venous pump. Other calf muscles also aid venous return.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which quadriceps muscle extends the knee and flexes the hip?
questions.note: Rectus femoris crosses both hip and knee. The vasti cross the knee only. The same question is repeated more clearly as Q29 on PDF page 13.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which is a factor in proximal-distal growth of a limb?
questions.note: AER-derived FGF signaling maintains distal outgrowth. Retinoic acid contributes to proximal identity but AER is the expected growth-center answer; ZPA patterns the anteroposterior axis.
questions.subject: embryology

questions.prompt: Which ligaments connect adjacent vertebral laminae?
questions.note: Ligamenta flava link adjacent laminae. The longitudinal ligaments follow vertebral bodies; the cruciform ligament stabilizes the dens/craniovertebral junction.
questions.subject: anatomy
evidence: /study/reviews/cvs.pdf#page=11 — CVS spinal reference; no exact section in the limbs PDF.

questions.prompt: Which vessel pierces the oblique popliteal ligament?
questions.note: The middle genicular artery, from popliteal artery, penetrates the posterior capsule/oblique popliteal ligament to supply intra-articular structures including cruciate ligaments.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of these muscles receive obturator nerve supply except:
questions.note: Obturator internus is supplied by the nerve to obturator internus from the sacral plexus. Obturator externus, despite its similar name, is obturator supplied.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Fusion of which processes forms the lateral sacral crest?
questions.note: Lateral sacral crests represent fused transverse processes. Intermediate crests correspond to articular processes and the median crest to spinous processes. Repeated on PDF page 16.
questions.subject: anatomy
evidence: /study/reviews/cvs.pdf#page=9 — CVS spinal reference; no exact section in the limbs PDF.

questions.prompt: Which pair are the principal invertors of the foot?
options: Flexor hallucis longus and tibialis posterior
Flexor digitorum longus and tibialis anterior
Flexor hallucis longus and flexor digitorum longus
questions.note: Tibialis anterior and posterior are the main invertors, acting on opposite sides of the ankle's plantarflexion-dorsiflexion axis while both pull medially.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which listed combination characterizes a lumbar vertebra?
options: Bifid spinous process and small triangular vertebral canal
Large round vertebral canal and mammillary process
Transverse foramen and large round vertebral canal
Accessory process and quadrangular spinous process
questions.note: Lumbar vertebrae have accessory and mammillary processes and broad quadrangular spinous processes. Their vertebral foramen is triangular, so the round canal in B is incorrect despite the true mammillary feature.
questions.subject: anatomy
evidence: /study/reviews/cvs.pdf#page=9 — CVS spinal reference; no exact section in the limbs PDF.

questions.prompt: Name the abnormalities shown in B and C, respectively.
options: B: spina bifida occulta; C: myelomeningocele
B: myelomeningocele; C: spina bifida occulta
questions.note: B shows protruding meninges/CSF with the cord remaining in the canal (meningocele). In C, neural tissue is included in the protrusion (myelomeningocele). The original B/C figure is retained, cropped to exclude the selected answer.

questions.prompt: Which structure continues the lateral lip of the linea aspera proximally?
questions.note: The lateral lip continues proximally as the gluteal tuberosity. The medial lip continues into the spiral line; the pectineal line is intermediate.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle passes through the greater sciatic foramen?
questions.note: Piriformis leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen. Obturator internus tendon uses the lesser sciatic foramen. The piriformis question repeats on PDF page 22.
questions.subject: anatomy
